questions.prompt: What is the norm squared of [1/2, 1/2]^T?

options.text: Add the entries to get a probability
Set the second entry to zero

questions.explanation: The norm is 1/sqrt(2), so dividing by it multiplies both entries by sqrt(2).
The first column of H is [1,1]^T/sqrt(2), which is |+>.
Multiplying H by the plus vector adds in the first output and cancels in the second, giving |0>.

questions.prompt: What is the inner product of |0> and |1>?
questions.explanation: The basis vectors are orthogonal, so their inner product is zero.

questions.prompt: Why must an ideal quantum gate preserve a vector's norm?

options.text: To keep total probability equal to one

questions.explanation: A valid state must remain normalized, so a valid ideal gate must preserve norm.

questions.prompt: What does the angle of a complex amplitude represent?
questions.explanation: On the complex plane, angle represents phase and distance represents magnitude.
